title: Ansel and the Witness
premise: Noor Vane, the reclusive archivist of Saint Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent years cataloguing deaths in the city's cold-case ledgers while hiding behind the cathedral's locked crypt and a carefully erased past. When a nervous stranger pays a fortune in advance to prove that a murder listed in her own archive hasn't happened yet, Noor realizes someone is using her files as a blueprint for killing — and that the future victim may be connected to the family she abandoned decades ago. As she infiltrates the investigation alongside weary Detective Ilsa Brandt, Noor discovers the client is her presumed-dead brother, who staged his own death to escape their father's crimes and now needs her help faking one more. In the end, Noor must choose between preserving her invisibility and testifying as the sole witness to what really happened in the crypt twenty years ago, trading her anonymity for a found family among the living.
about_author: P. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years transcribing burial registers before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who hide inside institutions, and they still cannot walk past a locked church door without wondering what's behind it.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Ends
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Establishes her ritual: cataloguing deaths by candlelight in the cathedral archive, her only companions the crypt lock and a cat named Marginalia. A letter arrives with an impossible commission. Beat: controlled loneliness cracked by curiosity.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The client, calling himself Mr. Sallow, pays triple to prove the 1998 death of 'E. Vane' hasn't happened yet. The name is hers — or nearly. She almost refuses; the money buys silence from creditors. Beat: dread disguised as greed.

chapters.title: Cold Ink
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She pulls the file on E. Vane and finds her own handwriting on pages she never wrote — dated next week. Someone has forged her archival hand with unsettling precision. Beat: violation of the one sanctuary she trusted.

chapters.title: Detective Brandt Hates Churches
chapters.summary: Ilsa Brandt's POV. Introduce the detective reopening a string of deaths near the cathedral, all victims who once testified in old trials. She visits the archive; Noor lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. Beat: two keepers of secrets circling.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Flashback woven in: twenty years ago, the night her father died in the crypt and her brother Elias vanished, presumed drowned. Noor changed her name and buried herself in the church. Beat: grief shown as inventory.

chapters.title: A Murder With a Deadline
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Cross-referencing recent deaths against the forged file, Noor finds each victim was killed exactly as predicted, days after the entries appeared. The next entry names a date four days out. Beat: the mystery becomes a countdown.

chapters.title: The Witness List
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt maps the victims: all witnesses from the 2004 trial of Aldous Vane, the cathedral's disgraced benefactor. She suspects a survivor finishing the job. Beat: institutional pressure to close the case fast.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Someone has been inside the archive — dust disturbed, a page dog-eared at the exact entry. Noor rigs a trap of flour and thread, archivist-style. Beat: paranoia sharpening into agency.

chapters.title: Four Days
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The trap catches not the killer but a terrified young verger, Tam, who admits he was paid to copy pages — by a man whose voice he can't describe but whose ring he can draw. Beat: first ally, first guilt.

chapters.title: The Ring With the Broken Seal
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt recognizes Tam's sketch: a signet from the Vane estate, officially destroyed. Her captain orders her off anything touching the Vane name. Beat: the case grows teeth above her pay grade.

chapters.title: Elias, Drowned
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor visits the riverbank where Elias supposedly drowned and finds fresh flowers, replaced weekly, for twenty years. Someone never believed he died either. Beat: hope she doesn't dare feel.

chapters.title: Entry Number Nine
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A new forged entry appears overnight: the next victim will be Tam. Noor breaks her cardinal rule and calls Brandt directly. Beat: isolation ending, stakes personal.

chapters.title: Safe House of Stone
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Noor hides Tam in the crypt itself — the one place even police need her permission to enter. Brandt notices Noor knows the crypt too well. Beat: trust built on mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Surveillance footage shows 'Mr. Sallow' entering the cathedral but never leaving. Brandt confronts Noor, who admits the commission. Uneasy alliance formalized over bad coffee. Beat: confession without revelation.

chapters.title: Father's Papers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Digging into sealed records, Noor finds her father Aldous was blackmailing half the city from the crypt — and the witness list were those who helped bury him. Beat: the past reorganizes itself around a darker shape.

chapters.title: Tam Talks
chapters.summary: Tam's POV (first time). Tam describes the voice: soft, patient, quoting scripture wrong on purpose — the way Elias used to tease Noor. She refuses to believe it. Beat: denial as armor.

chapters.title: The Date Arrives
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The predicted murder day passes; Tam lives. Either the killer was watching them — or the entry was bait to flush Noor out. Beat: relief curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Sallow Unmasked
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Following the flower trail, Noor sets a meeting and comes face to face with Elias — alive, older, wearing their father's ring. He paid her to investigate because only she could read the forger's hand. Beat: reunion as ambush.

chapters.title: What Elias Did
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Twenty years ago Elias didn't drown; he killed their father in self-defense during the blackmail confrontation, and Noor, half-asleep, saw everything. He fled so her testimony would die with her memory. Beat: the reveal reframes every prior chapter.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Elias swears he isn't killing the witnesses — he's been receiving the same forged predictions, warning him away. Someone else learned the family secret and is erasing everyone who could confirm it. Beat: hunter and hunted swap places.

chapters.title: Two Files, One Hand
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt independently concludes the murders mimic the 2004 trial evidence point by point — someone is executing the case file itself. The killer isn't hiding the truth; they're performing it. Beat: intellectual horror.

chapters.title: The Third Vane
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Records reveal a third child, unmentioned: a ward Aldous kept in the crypt's annex, raised on his papers. Noor remembers a shadow she was told was a draft. Beat: family expands into nightmare.

chapters.title: Annex
chapters.summary: Noor and Elias, joint POV. They break into the walled annex and find a room preserved like a shrine: schoolwork, newspaper clippings of the trial, and practice sheets covered in perfect imitations of Noor's handwriting. Beat: pity and terror entwined.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The ward, now grown, works in the cathedral offices under another name. Wren narrates a childhood of learning that love was transactional and that the Vanes erased people. Wren believes eliminating the witnesses completes Father's last instruction. Beat: antagonist humanized, logic made chillingly coherent.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confesses to Noor that he let her believe him dead to protect himself, not her — survival made him a coward. Noor's fury is the chapter's engine. Beat: found family tested at its root.

chapters.title: Brandt Closes In
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt identifies Wren through the office employment rolls and requests backup; her captain stalls, revealing someone above him is protecting the Vane legacy. Beat: the institution itself compromised.

chapters.title: Night Office
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren realizes Brandt is close and begins burning the forged files — including, painfully, the practice sheets, the only record of being seen. Beat: villain grieving their own erasure.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor offers Wren a trade via dead drop: the original 2004 testimony Noor secretly kept, in exchange for stopping. Wren counters: come to the crypt alone, bring the testimony, or Tam dies. Beat: trap accepted knowingly.

chapters.title: What Noor Saw
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Preparing to testify if she survives, Noor finally says aloud what she witnessed as a child — her father's death, Elias's hand, her own silence sold for safety. Beat: theme crystallized; memory as debt.

chapters.title: Locks
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Noor enters the crypt; Wren seals the door with the original key, meaning to stage Elias's long-promised death and end the ledger. Brandt, tipped by Tam, races across the close. Beat: claustrophobic ascent of tension.

chapters.title: The Crypt Trial
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Wren puts the Vanes on trial among the tombs, reading Father's instructions aloud. Noor doesn't argue innocence — she offers witness: 'I saw you. You were a child. So was I.' Beat: empathy as disarmament.

chapters.title: Elias Descends
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias gives himself up through the crypt's iron grate, offering the confession Wren actually wants — acknowledgment, not murder. Wren wavers between completing the pattern and breaking it. Beat: climax hinge.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt forces the crypt's secondary entrance through the ossuary, lights and noise flooding the sacred dark. Wren panics; a struggle; Noor takes a blade meant for Elias. Beat: physical climax, sacrifice.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, hospital-framed. From a gurney, Noor gives full statement: the father's crimes, Elias's act, her own silence, Wren's manufacture. The price of survival, itemized. Beat: catharsis through precision.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Wren, spared a murder conviction for Tam's aborted killing, receives treatment and years; Elias confesses to manslaughter and accepts prison. Brandt closes the file and resigns rather than bury the captain's role. Beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Unlocking the Crypt
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The cathedral chapter, scandal exposed, opens the crypt to the public. Noor catalogs its contents honestly for the first time, including the annex, preserved now as testimony rather than shrine. Beat: secrecy transformed into stewardship.

chapters.title: Visiting Hours
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor visits Elias in prison; their conversations are stilted but real. He asks why she came. 'You're the only person who remembers me before,' she says. Beat: forgiveness begun, not finished.

chapters.title: Found
chapters.summary: Ensemble moments. Tam returns to the archive as Noor's apprentice; Brandt takes pie at the verger's table; Wren writes letters Noor answers. The found family assembles awkwardly around tea. Beat: warmth earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor writes the final ledger entry herself — her own name, her true name, date of birth, 'status: alive' — and files it where anyone might find it. Beat: invisibility voluntarily ended.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Witness
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, coda. Revealed: 'Ansel' was the name her father gave the shadow-child, and Noor has been signing her letters to Wren with it — the sibling name returned. On the cathedral steps, spring light, Marginalia asleep on the ledger. Beat: quiet, complete resolution.
